newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: EIB to grant 30mln ECU loan for Slovak gas utility.
newsitem.headline: EIB to grant 30mln ECU loan for Slovak gas utility.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) will sign a 30 million ECU loan for Slovak state monopoly gas distributor Slovensky Plynarensky Priemysel (SPP) s.p. by the end of the year, a Slovak daily said on Tuesday.
"The EIB will sign a 30 million ECU loan with the SPP by the end of this year," daily Hospodarske Noviny quoted EIB Vice-president Wolfgang Roth as saying.
Neither the interest rate nor the maturity of the loan was reported and SPP officials were not immediately available for comment.

Roth said future EIB activities in Slovakia would also include a loan for motorway construction, particulary for financing road links between the Slovak capital Bratislava and neighbouring Hungary and Austria.
"The second credit will be of about the same size as the SPP loan," said Roth, declining to elaborate.
Roth did not specify what sort of gurantees had been given for the SPP loan but he said that the loan "would be guaranteed also by some non-state subjects."

Last week the EIB signed a 15-year, 70 million ECU loan for the Slovak state monopoly electricity utility, Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. (SE), to help finance the refurbishment of a power plant at Vojany in eastern Slovakia.
The credit, with no state guarantees, is expected to be followed by another 65 million ECU tranche from the EIB for the same project, planned for the period 1999 to 2002.
Roth said the EIB's strategy was to end requirements for state guarantees for loans in Slovakia by 2001, with the exception of credits for highway and railway construction.
